set.approach: Walk up alongside the creek, past the culvert, and pick up the flagged trail that heads toward the cliffs. When you reach the boulder field, angle up and right across it, then keep to the trail beyond three smaller, chossy cliffs until you arrive at the one worth climbing. Inhale Deeply begins on a grubby ledge over Spray some on yourself. The ledge can be reached by walking down or rappelling from the Tastes like Tabasco anchor, by taking a belay from the Spray some on your friends anchor, or by the short ramp on the right. Clip into the bottom anchor, then head up the obvious bolt line toward a dihedral.
set.descent_text: The two-bolt anchor is fitted with a rap ring for getting down.

review.notes: Area page: approach; route page: start ledge and access, anchor with rap ring.

set.approach: Drive about halfway through Red Rock Canyon, round the bend where the big red debris pile comes nearest the road, and use any pullout past it. Look east toward the canyon rim for a prominent ridge that reaches the canyon floor with very little bushwhacking, and hike it to the rim. From the west rim, cross the tundra plateau to the east rim, where the alpine lake below Canwell Peak comes into view. The crags are a little south of there, closer to the peak, on top of the plateau. Gunshot takes the crag's steepest ground, left of Power Outage.

review.notes: Area page: full approach; route page: steepest line left of Power Outage. Approach time left out. No descent stated.

set.approach: Climb the slope right of Southeast Buttress until you are just beneath East Tower. Walking up from below, the Razorback climbs are on the formation's right, and Razorblade is the only bolted line on it.

review.notes: Area page: approach; route page: right side, only bolted line. Top-rope setup via a neighbouring route is not used. No descent stated.

set.approach: Use the second 11 Mile pullout, on the west side of the road. Head north along the road to the point where the roadside cliff gives way to forest, and push into the trees; tall boots help when the river runs high. Follow a vague trail along the hillside to a new talus field of rocks cleared from the face above, where a vague trail leads to a belay stance with a single bolt. Approach up the scree to the right of the formation rather than on the soil directly under it. Find the belay bolt on top of the shrubs to start.

review.notes: Area page: parking and trail; route page: scree to the right, belay bolt on the shrubs. No descent stated.

set.approach: Starting at Spruce cabin, follow the approach trail and scramble over boulders northward to the first beach, going by the first gully that drains Waterfall Tower. Skirt the overgrowth to the second beach and climb the obvious gully that descends from the base of the Apron. The boulder holding the route is in the woods on your right a few minutes up the gully; if you missed it, you are in the wrong gully.

review.notes: Area page: approach; route page: boulder on the right of the gully. No descent stated.

set.approach: Take the trail up to the boulders. From there you can climb straight to the wall, or bear up and right onto a trail running along the boulder field's right edge, which sidesteps the loose rock and moss and ends at the base of Chest Fur. The routes run to the right from there. Back Fur follows Chest Fur for seven bolts, then goes right before the wide crack. Be careful on the ledge, which has loose rocks and dirt.

review.notes: Area page: approach; route page: variant of Chest Fur, anchor. The descent line is thin; anchor use only. Lead review dropped the descent: it described top-roping, not getting down.
